Do NOT globally deduplicate these.

They belong to multiple learning patterns and should remain in each appropriate category.

- Easy
- Medium
- Hard

1-3 Easy
4-7 Medium
8-9 Hard

{
  id: 1,
  title: "Two Sum",
  category: "Arrays",
  difficulty: "Easy"
}

Use the actual LeetCode difficulty for every problem.

If difficulty metadata is not currently available, create a centralized problem metadata dataset and populate the verified difficulty values rather than generating them randomly.

====================================================
5. PROBLEM UI
====================================================

[checkbox]

#1  Two Sum

EASY     O(N)     Arrays     HashMap

Example:

[ ] #1 Two Sum
    EASY   O(N)   Arrays   HashMap

[ ] #26 Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
    EASY   O(N)   Arrays   Two Pointers

[ ] #53 Maximum Subarray
    MEDIUM   O(N)   Arrays   DP

Do NOT display:

Problem 1 - Arrays

====================================================
6. LEETCODE LINK
====================================================

Each problem should have a deterministic LeetCode link:

https://leetcode.com/problems/<slug>/

Generate the slug from the actual problem title where appropriate.

Example:

Two Sum
→ https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum/

Maximum Subarray
→ https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-subarray/

The link should open in a new tab.

====================================================
7. PROGRESS SYSTEM
====================================================

The checkbox must be functional.

When a user marks:

Two Sum → solved

store that progress against the authenticated user.

Progress MUST NOT be hardcoded.

Progress must survive:

- page refresh
- logout/login
- navigation
- browser restart

Use the existing backend/database/auth architecture.

Do NOT use localStorage as the source of truth for solved DSA problems.

localStorage may only be used as an optional temporary cache.

Database/backend = source of truth.

====================================================
8. CATEGORY PROGRESS
====================================================

For each DSA category calculate:

Solved / Total

Example:

Arrays
4 / 17 solved

Strings
2 / 12 solved

HashMap
5 / 16 solved

And overall:

DSA Progress
11 / TOTAL solved

Percentage must be calculated dynamically.

Do NOT hardcode:

"0 of 12 cleared"

if the actual roadmap contains hundreds of problems.

====================================================
9. ROADMAP HEADER
====================================================

The current page currently shows something like:

Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA)

280 / 412 problems solved

This number must be generated from the actual dataset.

Do NOT hardcode 280 / 412.

Use:

totalProblems = dataset.length
solvedProblems = user's completed problem records.length

percentage = solvedProblems / totalProblems * 100

====================================================
10. CATEGORY ORDER
====================================================

Display the learning categories in a structured progression.

Recommended order:

01 Arrays
02 Strings
03 HashMap / HashSet
04 Two Pointers
05 Sliding Window
06 Prefix Sum
07 Sorting

The UI should preserve this order.

====================================================
11. DO NOT CHANGE THE EXISTING DESIGN
====================================================

Keep the existing StudyHub visual language.

Do NOT redesign the page.

Do NOT change:

- header
- navbar
- grid background
- typography
- cards
- colors
- spacing
- sidebar structure
- existing roadmap layout

Only replace the incorrect placeholder data and wire the page to the real DSA dataset.

====================================================
12. DATA ARCHITECTURE
====================================================

For example:

data/dsaRoadmap.ts

or the project's existing equivalent.

Structure:

{
  categoryId: "arrays",
  categoryName: "Arrays",
  problems: [
    {
      id: 1,
      title: "Two Sum",
      difficulty: "Easy",
      tags: ["Arrays", "HashMap"],
      leetcodeSlug: "two-sum"
    }
  ]
}

The UI must consume this dataset.

DO NOT duplicate problem data across components.

====================================================
13. VERIFY THE IMPLEMENTATION
====================================================

Before saying the task is complete:

1. Search the entire codebase for "Problem 1".
2. Search for "Problem 2".
3. Search for `"Problem ${`.
4. Search for placeholder DSA data.
5. Confirm there are ZERO placeholder problem titles.
6. Confirm every displayed problem has:
   - LeetCode ID
   - actual title
   - actual difficulty
   - category
7. Confirm the total count is dynamically calculated.
8. Confirm solved progress is dynamically calculated.
9. Confirm progress survives refresh.
10. Run TypeScript checks.
11. Run production build.

IMPORTANT:

DO NOT JUST FIX THE FIRST 10 CARDS.

The ENTIRE DSA ROADMAP must use the actual curated dataset.

====================================================

/roadmaps?module=dsa

#1 Two Sum
#26 Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
#27 Remove Element
#53 Maximum Subarray
#88 Merge Sorted Array

Do not patch the UI with string replacements.

Trace where the DSA problem list originates and replace the underlying placeholder dataset with the canonical curated DSA roadmap dataset.
One important thing
Your screenshot also shows:
280 / 412 problems solved

That is another red flag.
Our curated roadmap is not supposed to magically have 412 generic generated problems. The total should be calculated from the actual categories/problems we supplied.
So tell Antigravity explicitly:
"Do not make the UI look correct by changing the labels. Fix the underlying DSA dataset and make every count derive from that dataset."

That is the key fix.
